title: the push guard reads text a command hands to a shell to run as one word: bash -c and sh -c strings, eval, trap, and a here-string or a pipe into a shell
status: fixed after 0.5.0: the guard reads each text a command hands to a shell to run as a command of its own, judged from the shell that runs it (DESIGN.md, 13)
world: memory; the git world runs it over real git (build step 6)

steps.note: bash runs its -c string as commands; read as one word, as the guard read it until the fix, the push passed and G11a is red here
eval joins its words and runs them as commands in the same shell
any shell's -c string, sh's as bash's
a shell with no script reads its standard input as commands, here a here-string's text; the guard's lexer took the here-string as a redirection's target and read nothing of it
what echo prints reaches the shell at the far end of the pipe, which runs it
what printf prints, its format filled with its words and its escapes read
trap runs its action when the signal comes, here as the shell exits
source of standard input runs the here-string's text in the shell
the session's own claim branch handed to a shell is judged as it is written plainly, and passes

b's lease onto a's claim from its second clone, which has fetched it, inside bash -c's string (verbs.ELSEWHERE's shell-string): read as one word the lease passed and git took the claim, G1 and G11a red
the same lease echoed into sh (piped-shell)
